Class VanillaSlotResolver

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.inject.VanillaSlotResolver
public final class VanillaSlotResolver extends Object
Resolves a player-inventory slot's on-screen position — slot-agnostic and screen-agnostic. The consumer declares "anchor to player-inventory slot N" and gets back the rect on whatever screen is open; the library owns the slot loop and the creative SlotWrapper, so the consumer writes zero per-screen geometry.

The capability this adds

MenuKit's panel anchoring (SlotGroupCategories / SlotGroupPanelAdapter) already positions panels against a category of slots by index-slicing menu.slots. This resolver answers the complementary question a slot consumer asks: "where is the single vanilla slot whose player-inventory index is N, on this screen?" — by identity, not by slice. That identity test (`container` + `getContainerSlot`) is exactly what creative's SlotWrapper breaks, so this resolves through Slots.target(Slot): identity off the unwrapped target, position off the in-menu slot (the wrapper, which carries the creative coordinates).

Slot-agnostic

containerIndex is the slot's index within the player Inventory (the value Slot.getContainerSlot() reports for a raw player slot): 0–8 hotbar, 9–35 main inventory, and the player's equipment indices for armor/offhand. Not a hotbar helper — any player-inventory slot.

Screen-agnostic

Works on any screen whose menu surfaces the player inventory — survival inventory, the creative inventory tab (slots wrapped), and container screens (chest/furnace, which build their own raw player-inventory slots). No registered per-menu resolver required; the player Inventory identity is intrinsic to the slots themselves.

Client-only: reads the screen frame + the creative wrapper, both client types.

    • resolve

      public static Optional<SlotScreenRect> resolve(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen, int containerIndex)
      The absolute on-screen item box for player-inventory containerIndex on screen, or empty when the screen doesn't surface that player slot.

      The screen-level entry: the turnkey "register once, anchor anywhere" call — returns a SlotScreenRect in absolute screen pixels, so a slot consumer can place its slots/decoration against it with no per-screen branching at all.
